narrative.overview:
SQLSage's documentation is a terminal you can read. Every page sits inside a warm near-black console — serif prose for the reading voice, IBM Plex Mono for all the chrome — with a single green accent that means "correctness, active, go." The reader is never handed a brochure; they are handed a session. The topbar carries the two-tone sql·sage wordmark, the sidebar is a directory tree (docs/, ├── and └── glyphs), and every page opens with a psql-style breadcrumb: sqlsage=# \d docs.getting-started.

The density is quiet and ordered: one idea per card, tight mono headings, generous serif lines capped at ~62ch. Surfaces are flat, separated by tone and hairline rules rather than shadows or glow. Nothing flashes; the only motion is the terminal cursor's blink and the home demo's slow line-by-line reveal. Green is reserved for the accent — prompts, keywords, active nav, primary action — and amber appears only where the tool is flagging a wrong-result risk or safety warning.
keyCharacteristics: A console session as a reading experience, not a marketing page
Warm near-black void (#0d0c0a) with paper ink (#ede6d6)
Serif prose (Source Serif 4) inside mono chrome (IBM Plex Mono)
One green accent for correctness and action; amber for warnings only
Flat surfaces and hairline rules — no glow, no gradient, no light theme

rules.name: The Single-Accent Rule
rules.body: Green is the only accent color, and amber is the only alert color; the two never trade jobs and nothing decorative borrows either. A page that needs a second accent is a page the design system is already failing.

rules.name: The Console Voice Rule
rules.body: Anything machine-shaped — commands, badges, headings, tree, breadcrumb, terminal output, code, tables — is set in the mono stack; prose is the only serif. Headings are mono because they are comments a session would print.

rules.name: The Flat-Surface Rule
rules.body: No surface carries a static or hover shadow; no element uses gradient or glow. Elevation is a lighter surface tone, and state is a border or ink change — nothing floats.

dos: Do keep every surface flat and separate it with tone and hairline rules — never shadow, glow, or gradient.
Do set all machine-shaped type — headings, topbar, sidebar, breadcrumb, badges, code, tables, terminal, footer — in IBM Plex Mono, and all prose in Source Serif 4.
Do reserve Green for the single accent (correctness, active, primary action) and Amber exclusively for warnings and wrong-result alerts.
Do cap prose at ~62ch and keep the reading column narrow.
Do keep the world dark-only; there is no light theme.
Do honor prefers-reduced-motion — the terminal demo must render its full output instantly when reduced motion is requested.
donts: Don't add a second accent; Green is the only accent and Amber is alert-only.
Don't use gradient text, glow, or drop shadows anywhere.
Don't mix Inter back in — the world is IBM Plex Mono + Source Serif 4.
Don't let amber appear on anything that is not a warning or wrong-result alert.
